entities.summary: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque and the Blue Mosque refer to the same building — the Sultanahmet Camii in Istanbul. This entity represents the same sacred structure as the blue-mosque entry above. See that entry for the full description of the mosque built by Sultan Ahmed I between 1609-1616 CE, famous for its six minarets, 20,000 İznik tiles, and position facing Hagia Sophia in Istanbul's historic center.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque) represents the culmination of Ottoman mosque architecture, its six minarets and İznik tile interior establishing the standard for Islamic monumental architecture.
